launches.title: Kanopy - spatial intelligence for physical infrastructure
launches.tagline: We monitor critical infrastructure using only video
launches.body:
TL;DR: Utilities plan operations using field data that can be years out of date. Kanopy uses computer vision to turn ordinary video into a 3D model of the grid, helping teams map tree risks, assess asset condition, and plan maintenance. We’ve already deployed across thousands of miles of power lines.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VFx7_ZF07nI>

**The problem**

There are roughly 100 million miles of above-ground linear infrastructure worldwide. The electricity grid alone accounts for \~60 million miles (equivalent to 2,500 times around the equator). Infrastructure is aging, the cost of failure is higher than ever, and the systems we rely on are too vast to monitor manually.

For utilities, vegetation management makes this challenge concrete. Arborists patrol power lines to identify dangerous trees and determine what needs cutting. Contractors estimate the work using manual surveys and historical averages. Once crews finish trimming, utilities send people back to verify the work. \
Planning the work and executing these multiple inspections take millions in spent resources.

**What Kanopy does**

Kanopy turns ordinary video from any camera into a detailed 3D model of the grid. The video can come from a drone, a GoPro on a truck, or simply from an iPhone shot.\
Our models measure vegetation clearances, identifies hazards, and assesses asset condition. Utilities use these insights to prioritize maintenance, plan fieldwork, and verify completed work. Each new drive or flight can refresh that picture using cameras teams already own.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125913&key=user_uploads/4010388/8d098664-36f4-487c-8c3d-ff9160ba2dc0)

**The team**

We’re Yann and Nicolas Pfitzer, brothers and founders of Kanopy

Yann spent more than five years at McKinsey as a Junior Partner working with utilities and energy companies\
Nicolas brings computer vision and robotics experience from work at ShapeScale (YC15), ETH Zürich, and research at University of Cambridge.
